# Findings

One file per measurement that shaped a decision, newest first. `verdict` is the whole result — open the file for the method.

| Date | Finding | Status | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-26 | [The preview budgets are decode budgets until the store is warm](2026.07.26-the-preview-budget-is-a-decode-budget.md) | open | A cold preview render costs ~22 ms per frame of `decode_range` and the filters are noise beside it, so `full_preview_render`'s 3 s ceiling is a limit of ~137 frames of footage — unmeetable on a 5-10 s window of the reference source by 2.2x to 4.4x. Warm, the same window re-renders after a parameter edit in 3.3 ms and the same budget is met with a 900x margin. The budgets therefore describe a warm preview, and what makes them reachable at all is the store surviving the edit, not any filter being fast. |
| 2026-07-26 | [A stateful filter's output is not keyed by what it is](2026.07.26-stateful-output-is-not-keyed-by-what-it-is.md) | closed | A stateful filter with a correct `warmup_frames` *is* span-independent to within its own declared epsilon — so the reason it may not be cached is not that its output varies, but that nothing can check the declaration the invariance rests on, and the key carries neither the declaration nor the run's origin. |
| 2026-07-25 | [The seek is irreducible](2026.07.25-the-seek-is-irreducible.md) | closed | set(POS_FRAMES) is 46.7 ms of a 67.8 ms round trip and has no tunable knob; hardware acceleration does not engage in this build and keyframe alignment buys nothing, so the budget is met by asking for less rather than decoding faster. |
| 2026-07-25 | [The filter contract cannot type what VISION asks filters to do](2026.07.25-the-filter-contract-cannot-type-vision.md) | closed | Three things VISION requires of filters are inexpressible in `FilterSpec`: tabular output, a change of frame rate, and output size. The rate gap is the expensive one — it makes ARCHITECTURE's warmup arithmetic silently wrong by the decimation factor across any decimating node. |
| 2026-07-25 | [The replicate crop is a spatial warmup, and nothing declares it](2026.07.25-the-crop-is-a-spatial-warmup.md) | superseded | WRONG IN ITS PREMISE — see `superseded_by`. It assumed the filter graph would run on uncropped parent frames until the crop materialized. It runs on the crop from the first frame; the parent is only where that crop is read from. The analysis of the two filter classes below is still correct and is what made the premise worth checking, but the consequence it drew does not follow. |
| 2026-07-25 | [The crop belongs in the graph, so materializing it cannot change a result](2026.07.25-the-crop-belongs-in-the-graph.md) | closed | The filter graph consumes the replicate's ROI crop from its first frame; the background crop is a faster source for the same pixels, never a switch in what is computed. That makes it a checkpoint, and `Project.checkpoints` is already contractually never hashed — so the whole-frame-statistic hazard is closed by an invariant the artifact had rather than by a new declaration. |
| 2026-07-25 | [Open to first frame has headroom](2026.07.25-open-to-first-frame-has-headroom.md) | closed | 213 ms against a 500 ms budget through the full GUI path — 25 ms of container metadata and 188 ms of first decode — so open is the one pre-pipeline budget with room to spare. |
| 2026-07-25 | [Decode cost is colour conversion](2026.07.25-decode-cost-is-colour-conversion.md) | closed | grab() is 1.3 ms and retrieve() is 29 ms, so almost all per-frame cost is the YUV to BGR convert — short forward jumps should grab rather than seek, and real-time playback of 59.94 fps 5.3K footage is not achievable at 34 fps decode. |
| 2026-07-25 | [Coalescing bounds scrub lag](2026.07.25-coalescing-bounds-scrub-lag.md) | closed | A burst of 40 seeks settles on the final target in 172 ms — roughly two decodes, not forty — so scrub latency is bounded by one decode regardless of drag speed; queued, the same burst would take ~3.2 s. |

*9 entries.*
